question: During which specific phase of the cell cycle does DNA replication occur?
explanation: The synthesis or S phase is dedicated entirely to replicating the cell's genetic material prior to division. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary function of cell cycle checkpoints?

options.A: To accelerate the production of metabolic energy
options.B: To halt division and allow for DNA damage repair
options.C: To permanently lock the cell in the mitotic phase
options.D: To stimulate rapid and unregulated tissue growth

explanation: Checkpoints serve as surveillance mechanisms that pause the cycle to detect and correct errors before replication proceeds. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which cellular adaptation describes the reversible replacement of one adult cell type by another?
explanation: Metaplasia occurs when chronic stress prompts tissue to substitute a hardier cell type for a more vulnerable one. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h2)

question: A patient's biopsy report indicates disordered cellular growth with significant variation in nuclear size and shape, categorized as a pre-malignant lesion. Which term best fits this description?
explanation: Dysplasia denotes disordered growth and loss of uniformity, representing an intermediate step toward malignancy. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes a malignant tumor from a benign tumor?

options.B: Cells that closely resemble the tissue of origin
options.C: The ability to metastasize to distant sites
options.D: A very slow and predictable growth rate

explanation: Metastasis is the hallmark of malignancy, allowing cancer cells to invade blood vessels and establish secondary colonies elsewhere in the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h3)

question: A histopathology report describes a tumor as having poorly differentiated cells with irregular borders and deep infiltration into adjacent muscular layers. How should this neoplasm be classified?
explanation: Poor differentiation and local tissue invasion are definitive indicators of a malignant neoplasm. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h3)

question: What defines the unique capability of stem cells known as self-renewal?

options.A: The rapid conversion of mature somatic cells into fully functional neurons
options.B: The ability to undergo numerous divisions while maintaining an unspecialized state
options.C: The transformation of malignant tissues into benign structural counterparts
options.D: The spontaneous induction of programmed cell death when DNA is damaged

explanation: Self-renewal ensures that the stem cell pool remains replenished throughout the life of the organism while continuously supplying differentiated progeny. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do cancer stem cells pose a significant challenge in oncology treatment?

options.A: They lose all capacity for cell division once primary treatment begins
options.B: They frequently survive conventional therapies and drive tumor recurrence
options.C: They secrete chemical signals that convert malignant cells into benign ones
options.D: They undergo rapid apoptosis upon exposure to pharmaceutical agents

explanation: Cancer stem cells often exhibit high resistance to chemotherapy and radiation, allowing them to regenerate the tumor even after apparent clinical remission. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary underlying cause of genetic alterations in cancer cells?

options.A: Excessive production of normal structural proteins by ribosomes
options.B: Inactivation of all metabolic pathways within mitochondria
options.C: Permanent cessation of the cell cycle during the G1 phase
options.D: Accumulation of DNA mutations in somatic cells over time

explanation: Cancer arises from sequential genetic mutations that disrupt normal cell cycle controls and DNA repair mechanisms. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: What clinical implication arises from tumor heterogeneity during chemotherapy?

options.A: All cancer cells within the tumor mass respond identically to the medication
options.B: Certain sub-populations of cancer cells may be resistant to the drug and survive
options.C: Metastasis becomes completely impossible due to genetic stabilization
options.D: The tumor will spontaneously convert into a benign, self-limiting growth

explanation: Because different cells within the same tumor have distinct mutations, targeted therapies may kill some cells while drug-resistant variants survive and proliferate. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the normal physiological role of proto-oncogenes in healthy tissue?

options.A: To induce immediate programmed cell death upon detecting DNA errors
options.B: To halt the cell cycle when chromosomal damage is irreparable
options.C: To replace damaged epithelial cells with fibrous connective tissue
options.D: To encode proteins that stimulate normal cell growth and division

explanation: Proto-oncogenes are essential normal genes that regulate positive growth signaling until mutations convert them into hyperactive oncogenes. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h6)

question: According to the two-hit hypothesis, why do most hereditary cancer syndromes require inactivation of both gene alleles?

options.A: A single functional copy of a tumor suppressor gene is often sufficient to maintain normal cell cycle control
options.B: Immune surveillance destroys cells that have only lost one copy of a regulatory gene
options.C: Both alleles must be amplified simultaneously to induce rapid cellular differentiation
options.D: Oncogenes require double mutations to prevent normal apoptotic pathways from engaging

explanation: Tumor suppressors are recessive at the cellular level, meaning both copies must be knocked out before their growth-restraining function is lost. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which key group of enzymes acts as the primary executioner cascade during apoptosis?
explanation: Caspases are proteolytic enzymes that systematically break down cellular proteins during programmed cell death. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of apoptosis?

options.A: Systematic and energy-dependent dismantling of cellular proteins
options.B: Spillover of cellular contents causing local tissue inflammation
options.C: Controlled condensation of chromatin within the nucleus
options.D: Formation of membrane-bound apoptotic bodies for phagocytosis

explanation: Apoptosis is specifically designed to clear cells cleanly without spilling contents, which prevents the inflammation characteristic of accidental necrosis. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why do traditional cytotoxic chemotherapy agents frequently cause side effects such as alopecia and mucositis?

options.A: They selectively stimulate apoptosis in benign connective tissue throughout the body
options.B: They convert malignant cells into metaplastic tissue within the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: They indiscriminately target rapidly dividing healthy cells in hair follicles and mucosal linings
options.D: They permanently deactivate all stem cell niches located within the bone marrow

explanation: Conventional chemotherapy affects any rapidly proliferating tissue, leading to common toxicities in hair, skin, and mucosal surfaces. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h8)

question: How do modern targeted cancer therapies differ fundamentally from traditional cytotoxic chemotherapy?

options.A: Targeted therapies eliminate cancer by inducing rapid, uncontrolled necrosis in all tissues
options.B: Targeted therapies exclusively use radiation beams focused on the primary tumor capsule
options.C: Targeted therapies aim at specific molecular abnormalities in cancer cells rather than all dividing cells
options.D: Targeted therapies rely entirely on preventing the expression of normal proto-oncogenes

explanation: Targeted drugs block specific proteins or genes involved in cancer growth, reducing collateral damage to normal, healthy tissues compared to broad cytotoxic drugs. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h8)
